ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Two chords $A B$ and $A C$ are drawn into a circle with diameter $\mathrm{AD}. \angle B A C=60^{\circ}$, $\overline{A B}=24 \mathrm{~cm}$, $\mathrm{E}$ lies on $\mathrm{AC}$ so that $\overline{E C}=3 \mathrm{~cm}$, and $\mathrm{BE}$ is perpendicular to $\mathrm{AC}$. How long is the chord $\mathrm{BD}$?

method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate route. In right triangle ABE, AB=24 and angle BAE=60°, so AE=24 cos 60°=12 and BE=24 sin 60°=12√3. Since EC=3, C=(15,0), E=(12,0), and B=(12,12√3). Find the circumcenter O of triangle ABC by intersecting perpendicular bisectors: from A and C, O has x=15/2; using equality of distances to A and B gives O=(15/2,11√3/2). Because AD is a diameter and A is one endpoint, D is the point antipodal to A, so D=2O-A=(15,11√3). Then compute BD as the distance from B=(12,12√3) to D=(15,11√3): BD=√(3^2+(−√3)^2)=2√3 cm.
